item.description: DeepTutor is an open-source project from the HKUDS GitHub organization that bills itself as lifelong personalized tutoring, with documentation hosted at deeptutor.info and a separate page for collaboration inquiries. The README is still mostly logos and badges, so the underlying models and architecture aren't spelled out yet; developers curious about how AI tutoring products get built will have to watch the repo for technical details.

item.description: A developer on Juejin walks through 32 Claude Code Skills and 8 MCP servers they have personally tested, with screenshots of the setup running. For anyone pushing Claude Code beyond plain coding into a fuller workflow, the list serves as a ready-made configuration reference instead of assembling servers one by one from scratch.

item.description: Google has released Genie 4, which the headline frames as a genuine world model. Only the title is available here and the 36Kr article body isn't included; the linked page isn't summarized, so specs, release form, and availability beyond the headline can't be confirmed.

item.title: [infoq] GPT-6.1 Terra 发布：比旗舰快 3 倍，价格仅1/10！事实错误率暴降近 70%
item.description: OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra, an upgrade to GPT-5.6 Terra that halves the standard API price versus its predecessor and GPT-6.1 Sol, while costing about one tenth of flagship GPT-6 Astra per token on some professional tasks. OpenAI says it finishes tasks more than three times faster than Astra and Sol, and cuts the error rate on its hallucination-baiting prompts from 53.6% to 16.7% at low reasoning effort.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 一个 Alma 的 Android 客户端
item.description: After the Alma iOS client shipped with no Android roadmap, developer lazyeo wrote an open-source Android client against the desktop app's relay interface. It can't call the API on its own — it must connect to Alma running on your own computer, which is the point: picking work back up while away from the desk. The UI and colors follow the desktop build, it adapts to foldables, and it attempts a Duo-style blur, though Samsung hinges expose no live angle, so Shizuku permissions get it closer.

item.title: [infoq] 智能指数得分创新高！蚂蚁百灵开源Ling-3.1-flash-1019：让Personal Agent走向真实业务
item.description: Ant Group's Ling team open-sourced Ling-3.1-flash-1019, tuned for Personal Agent workloads such as multi-step tasks and complex workflows, scoring 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 — three points above the previous version. The base model Ling-3.1-flash-base was released alongside it: a hybrid linear MoE with roughly 560B total parameters and about 25B activated per token, reported to beat DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base and MiMo-V2.5-Pro-Base on 32 of 47 benchmarks.

item.title: [v2ex] [Claude] claude 又送重置了， 12 月 1 号前到期
item.description: A V2EX post says Claude has handed out another usage-limit reset, which expires before December 1. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 因为受够了手动更新 IIS 证书，我花了半年时间做了一个自动托管平台，想听听大家的意见
item.description: SSLThink is a certificate hosting and auto-deployment platform aimed at Windows Server + IIS, requesting Let's Encrypt certificates over ACME and pushing them to sites, with a web console for managing several servers instead of remoting into each one. The author built it after Aliyun and Tencent Cloud cut free certificate lifetimes from a year to six months and then three, making expiry easy to miss. Public beta pricing is 10 yuan per certificate per year.

item.title: [github_trending] Nutlope/hallmark
item.description: Hallmark is a design skill from Together AI that plugs into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode: it deals three themes from a 50-theme catalog, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, then lints the result in a real browser for AI tells such as eyebrows above every heading, tracked-capital labels, a hero that misses its screen, and a signup form that thanks you without sending anything. Gates run in tiers, with Floor never shipping and a fresh-context reviewer having the last wor

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 给 Codex 做了块画布，随手试了下，它一笔画完了一只猫
item.description: The developer of Galta built a web canvas that sits beside the page and links to agents such as Codex and Claude Code over MCP. Dragging in a meme of a cat in a suit and asking GPT-6-Astra to repaint it produced 620 editable vector strokes; a follow-up constraint to draw it without lifting the pen yielded one path of 70,722 points. It runs in Chrome and Dia, though AI connections currently need an Apple silicon Mac.

item.title: [v2ex] [OpenAI] Codex 额度消费偷偷长了点？
item.description: A V2EX poster reports that 12 hours of uninterrupted Codex use burned 9% of their quota on the 20x plan with the 6.1sol high-multiplier setting, suspecting consumption has crept up. The post is a single line with no screenshots, baseline comparison or official response, so it stands as one user's observation rather than a confirmed billing change.

item.title: [github_trending] elayadesign/ai-design-skills
item.description: ai-design-skills is a collection of design skills from elayadesign for AI coding tools that read markdown rule files, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Windsurf. Each skill is a self-contained folder you install individually; the first, landing-page-design, covers intake questions, page structure, conversion copy and a visual system of type, spacing, radius and motion. Useful if you want AI-generated pages to follow a consistent design standard.

item.title: [infoq] 轻量化异构双臂 × VLA/世界模型：家庭服务具身机器人的落地实践
item.description: Recorded at AICon Shenzhen 2026, this talk by 乐享科技 co-CTO and 穹明智能 GM 李元庆 covers home-service embodied robots: a lightweight heterogeneous dual-arm body, layered software architecture, a sim-to-real data loop, and how rule-based and modular-based policies cooperate versus where end-to-end methods fall short under real-hardware constraints. A “fetch me a glass of water” long-horizon task illustrates the difficulty. Automated code generation and a self-evolving RSI system are also discussed.

item.title: [infoq] Anthropic 内部系统被 AI Agent 12 小时攻破！会议记录、员工薪酬、内部模型讨论遭访问
item.description: A draft Cathedral report seen by The Washington Post says researchers running an AI agent needed under 12 hours to find a path into Anthropic's internal systems, exploiting a vulnerability in commercial software used by Anthropic and many other companies. Anthropic confirmed limited data in its sales, HR and IT systems was accessed, while Claude conversations, source code and model weights were untouched. Its monitoring had already caught some activity; the two sides dispute the disclosure proce

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] AI GIF Face Swap：上传照片和 GIF，按次付费生成换脸动图
item.description: AI GIF Face Swap takes one face photo plus a GIF, swaps the face in frame by frame, and returns an animated GIF; there is no sign-up, Stripe charges $1.99 per run, and each browser gets one free 3-second trial. It handles a single face only, caps GIFs at 720×720, 10 seconds and 150 frames, and does not touch video. Built on TanStack Start, Cloudflare Workers and Replicate.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 做了个 MiniCPM OCR 在线工具：把图片和 PDF 转成可编辑的文字、表格和公式
item.description: MiniCPM OCR is a web tool that takes images or PDFs and pulls out Chinese and English text, paragraphs and page layout, rebuilds table structure, and converts math into LaTeX. Results can be checked against the original, edited in place, and exported as Word, Markdown or JSON with region coordinates. It runs on OpenBMB's MiniCPM-OCR-1.0; the author notes messy tables, blurry scans and formulas still need a human pass.

item.title: [infoq] Claude Code 撑起史上最大 IPO，被封号不退费的中国开发者撑起那 5%“脏收入”
item.description: Anthropic's S-1, filed for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, puts Claude Code at the center of its enterprise story: the top 5% of Claude Code enterprise users spend roughly 20 times what non-users pay each month, and over 90% of codebase contributions in September 2026 were written by Claude. The filing also admits 5–7% of revenue comes from customers who broke usage rules, around $1.7–2.3B.

item.title: [infoq] 模型越来越强，落地却处处卡关？14位行业大佬拆解难题｜1024 模力工场 · AI社区日圆满收官
item.description: On October 24, Geekbang held its 1024 Moli Workspace AI Community Day at Yun Gu Center in Hangzhou, where 14 main-forum talks walked through real deployments and failure modes in office work, research, manufacturing and creation, alongside a 15-booth AI market and two hands-on workshops. The company also announced that its southern headquarters and TGO's global headquarters are now based in Hangzhou; organizers counted over 1,000 on-site visits.

item.title: [infoq] 尤雨溪团队推出 Vite+ 1.0：JavaScript 工具链迎来“大一统”？
item.description: VoidZero, now owned by Cloudflare, shipped Vite+ 1.0, a single vp CLI that manages the Node.js runtime, package manager and a stack of Vite 8, Vitest, Oxlint, Oxfmt, Rolldown and tsdown, all configured through one vite.config.ts; the MIT-licensed package sees close to 2 million weekly downloads. Work since beta focused on CI, migration and diagnostics, with setup-vp now covering GitLab CI/CD, vp migrate handling tsup projects, and Tiptap and Dify among adopters.

item.title: [v2ex] [硬件] 存储掉电时写缓存去哪了？以戴尔 Unity XT 为例，聊聊 BBU 和 M.2 为什么是关键件
item.description: A V2EX post digs through Dell's specs, whitepaper and hardware guide for the Unity XT 480 to explain what happens to write cache on power loss: the BBU powers the storage processor long enough to flush controller memory to an internal M.2 SSD before shutdown, and the same path runs when an SP itself fails. The author also flags that DPE slots 0-3 are fixed system disks and that I/O modules are mirrored, and asks how often others replace BBUs.

item.title: [infoq] Meta 利用私有处理技术将机密计算扩展至 AI 眼镜
item.description: Meta extended its Private Processing feature, previously used for WhatsApp and Meta AI, to AI glasses: sensitive workloads run inside confidential VMs backed by hardware TEEs, with remote attestation, anonymous credentials, OHTTP relays and encryption keeping user context inside the boundary, enough to support streaming transcription, contextual search and long-term memory recall. WIRED reports the shipping glasses don't have it yet, and Meta gave no timeline.

item.title: [hackernews] Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone
item.description: A Hacker News submission whose title states the team hacked exactly what it set out to hack: the iPhone. The post body repeats that single sentence, so there's no word on vulnerability class, iOS version, exploit chain, or vendor response, and it's unclear whether this was a live attack, a jailbreak, or a demo. The linked page isn't summarized here.

item.title: [infoq] 全国最大规模机器人App黑客松落幕：36小时跑通16款真机应用
item.description: On October 25, Astribot closed the finals of its Astribot OS (AOS) robot hackathon in Shenzhen, where 17 teams spent 36 hours building 16 robot apps and 94% of them ran on real hardware. AOS bundles perception, mobility and manipulation into composable Meta packages and Skills wired to models such as GPT-6 and DeepSeek, letting creators go from a one-line prompt to a working app without writing low-level code.

item.title: [hackernews] Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
item.description: A submission pointing to Kimi's code-model docs, which list two entries, K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed, plus an Artificial Analysis model page and a comparison blog on Chinese open-source AI. Only links were posted, so context length, pricing, and how Highspeed differs from the base model can't be determined from the submission itself.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin post on how 2026 technical interviews differ from two years ago: instead of hand-writing a Promise or explaining React Fiber, interviewers now assume candidates already use AI and ask why a company should still hire them when AI writes 80% of the code. It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

item.title: [hackernews] Evidence of a spying operation by ICE against left-wing social movements
item.description: A report alleges that ICE's Homeland Security Investigations is running far-reaching surveillance of left-wing activists, on a scale comparable to the FBI and CIA crackdowns on the Civil Rights and anti-war movements. This is a link post carrying only that description; the linked page isn't summarized here, so details on targets, methods and legal basis aren't available.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A developer writes up roughly half a month of using Codex after switching from Cursor. Cursor was what first made AI-assisted coding feel striking, he says, but Codex reads less like a coding assistant and more like a genuine super-agent, closer to the next stage of the tooling. Useful for anyone weighing an editor-integrated assistant against an agent-first workflow.

item.title: [hackernews] Microsoft offers mass buyouts for roughly a quarter of its workforce
item.description: A Hacker News submission states that Microsoft is offering mass buyouts to roughly a quarter of its workforce. The item is title-only with no body content, so which divisions are covered, what the packages include and any deadline are not available here.

item.title: [hackernews] US Government is hiding a secret court ruling about how it spies on Americans
item.description: Two US senators say the Trump administration is breaking the law by withholding a FISA court decision while pressing Congress to renew what the report calls America's most sweeping surveillance program. The clash matters because lawmakers are being asked to reauthorize the program without being able to see how the court has ruled on spying on Americans.

item.title: [github_trending] togg53192-cmd/jailbreaks
item.description: The GitHub repo togg53192-cmd/jailbreaks gathers 32 prompts aimed at more than 26 models, including full system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, AGENTS.md files and Ollama Modelfiles, each meant to be complete and paste-ready rather than excerpted. Coverage runs from free stealth models on OpenCode Zen and open-weight families like GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi and Qwen to closed models such as Claude, Gemini, Grok and Mistral. Aimed at people probing prompt boundaries and agent configuration.

item.title: [github_trending] pbakaus/impeccable
item.description: Impeccable is a design vocabulary for coding agents: install it with npx impeccable install, run /impeccable init inside your agent, and you get commands like polish, bolder, critique and audit to steer and review UI output, catching formulaic AI-generated design before it ships. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and other tools, and targets developers who care about visual quality.

item.title: [hackernews] Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
item.description: Eleven days after Apple was notified that the eMudhra certificate authority had been compromised, the git, curl and python3 binaries shipped with macOS still trust the affected certificates. Anyone pulling code or making TLS connections with those system tools stays exposed to interception until the root is removed by hand, so macOS developers should check their trust store.

item.title: [hackernews] Genie 4
item.description: Google DeepMind has introduced Genie 4, billed as a new generation of world simulation that generates interactive worlds users can explore. It sits in the same model lineup as Gemini, Veo and Lyria, alongside the earlier SIMA 2 agent work. Researchers working on world models, game generation or embodied-agent simulation are the obvious audience.

item.title: [github_trending] hmjz100/LinkSwift
item.description: LinkSwift is a JavaScript userscript, forked from the "Wangpan Direct Download Helper," that pulls direct download links out of eight Chinese cloud drives including Baidu, Aliyun, Quark and 123. Its README warns people who installed it from GreasyFork to overwrite it from another source, so a broken script still gets updates.

item.title: [github_trending] obra/superpowers
item.description: obra/superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology built on composable skills plus initial instructions your agent is meant to follow. Its README documents setup for many coding tools, including Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI. It targets developers who want their coding agent to follow a repeatable engineering process instead of improvising.

item.title: [github_trending] JetBrains/thinkrail
item.description: ThinkRail is a JetBrains incubator project: an agentic IDE built on the pi coding agent from the @earendil-works/pi npm package, wrapping it in a full interface, isolating each task in its own workspace, and giving the agent durable project knowledge through living specs and reusable skills. JetBrains says full extension support comes next, so the IDE can generate the tools it needs from how you actually work. It targets developers who want agents handling whole tasks rather than autocomplete.

item.title: [github_trending] nightly-labs/openbot
item.description: OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace from nightly-labs that gives each AI agent its own workspace and conversation, plus task queues, file transfer, an embedded browser and agent-to-agent messaging. It runs the Codex App Server and Claude Code natively and adds Grok CLI, Gemini, Cursor CLI and others over ACP. It suits developers juggling several coding agents, but it's a dev preview where agents run with full access and no approval prompts.

item.title: [zhihu] 外交部回应姆巴佩道歉，「我们重视当事人作出的道歉」，姆巴佩事件的后续走向还有哪些可能性？

item.description: Cindy is an Apache-2.0 open-source AI agent from makecindy that is meant to work out of the box. It links your work computer, home desktop, laptop and phone, uses the models and subscriptions you already pay for, and does real work on your own machines. It's aimed at developers who want a customizable, self-hosted agent without building the scaffolding themselves.

item.title: [juejin] 一键还原任意网站，这套 Playwright + 多 Agent 工程流太猛了
item.description: A Juejin post by author alien walks through ai-website-cloner-template, a project that recreates any website in one shot using Playwright plus a multi-agent pipeline. It covers both how to use the template and how it works internally, which makes it useful for developers exploring agent-driven browser automation or page cloning.

item.title: [juejin] DeepSeek Harness 值得安装的 15 款插件
item.description: With DeepSeek Harness (DSH) drawing a surge of attention, its community plugin ecosystem has grown quickly, and this post picks out 15 plugins the author considers worth installing. For developers already using DSH, it works as a pre-filtered shortlist instead of testing community add-ons one by one.

item.title: [juejin] 副业搞起来，小说，漫画，漫剧的成本优化思路
item.description: A Juejin post laying out cost-optimization ideas for a side business built on novels, comics and comic-style shorts, linking the GitHub project aiskyhub/novel_to_comic for turning novels into comics. It suits indie developers monetizing AI-generated content who need generation and inference costs to stay under their margins.

item.title: [juejin] 基于 Pi，我居然自己搞了一个好用的 AI Agent 桌面工作台
item.description: A Juejin post describes how the author built an AI Agent desktop workbench on top of Pi. Its main argument is not to reinvent the wheel: the model calls, message loop, tool protocol and permission system do not need to be written from scratch. It is aimed at developers who want their own agent desktop tool without rebuilding the plumbing first.

item.title: [juejin] 2028编程圈很火的10个Skills
item.description: The article lists 10 Skills it says are popular in the 2028 programming world, tracing how the question moved from "what is a Skill" two years earlier to Skills being treated as basic infrastructure for AI coding. Its framing is blunt: an AI coding assistant without Skills is like a browser without extensions.
